description: The Global Supply Chain Stress Index - Maritime (GSCSI-M) is a metric of global maritime supply chain disruption developed by the World Bank since 2021 and described in an open-access article in the Journal of Transport Geography (2026) by Jean-François Arvis, Jean-Paul Rodrigue, Daria Ulybina and Cordula Rastogi. It is derived from AIS vessel tracking data and computes the equivalent delayed capacity in twenty-foot equivalent units, at port, country, regional and global levels. The article uses it to quantify disruptions such as the COVID-19 pandemic (2021 to 2022), geopolitical incidents in the Red Sea and water shortages at the Panama Canal (2023 to 2024), and to explain surges in shipping rates on the assumption that shippers pay for scarce capacity. The port-level detail shows local bottlenecks and can inform targeted interventions and contingency planning. Coverage: global container shipping. Format and access: index series described in the article; the abstract does not give a download location. Licence and cost: the article is CC BY-NC-ND and free to read. Caveats: the abstract does not say whether the AIS inputs or the series are openly released. It supports resilience and capacity planning studies of maritime supply chains. It complements the Freightos Baltic Index, the ADB maritime passageway transit data and UNCTADstat maritime statistics in the catalogue.
